text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed quota attribution noise in the console after opt-in telemetry started rolling in from the new TS SDK. dashboard shows sudden tenant spikes. :eyes:
lee: Ugh. Can you paste an example? is it misattributing tokens to route=undefined or something else?
maya: Yep — a bunch of rows with `route: legacy` and `cost_center: unknown` for requests that should be tagged. small sample attached (sanitized).
lee: That suggests the header negotiation shim isn't consistently attached by older SDKs. Could be a race where SDK sends header later and proxy normalizes it to fallback.
tj: Which header are we talking about? `X-Client-Route` or the new `X-Rdwd-RouteMeta`?
maya: New one — `X-Rdwd-RouteMeta`. TS SDK 2.14 added it as opt-in flag `routeMeta: true`. Some clients turned it on and some didn't.
olivia: From PM side: customers see quota jumps and think we've changed pricing. Need a clear console UX and a rollback plan. We should surface "attribution confidence" in the quota tile rather than just raw numbers.
alex: Agree on confidence. Also we need a short-term mitigation: gate console rollup to only include attributions that meet minimal schema (route + tenant_id). everything else goes to "unknown attribution" bucket so it doesn't inflate specific route graphs.
rachel: I can add a small badge in the quota dashboard that shows % attributed vs unknown. That will help before we fix headers upstream.
lee: Long term we need header negotiation in the internal proxy: if we see legacy clients, attach placeholder metadata (but don't invent tenant ids). Better: API layer should attempt to synthesize route from auth token mapping when header missing, then mark it as synthesized.
tj: SDK-side fix: we'll add a backward-compatible handshake. Proposal:
```
// TS SDK
client = new RedwoodClient({
  routeMeta: { optIn: true, handshake: 'v1' }
})
// sends: X-Rdwd-RouteMeta-Negotiate: v1
```
If server responds with `X-Rdwd-Handshake-Ack: v1` we send full `X-Rdwd-RouteMeta`. Fallback: keep sending legacy header `X-Route` for 3 months.
lee: That sounds reasonable. How fast can you ship the handshake?
tj: I can do a minor release in 1 week, patch cherrypick for go/python SDKs as well. But we need a coordinated console flag so we don't flip graphs mid-release.
maya: Also need to think about quota reconciliation: historical data will be split. We should add a console view that overlays pre/post attribution and an option to normalize.
olivia: Good call. Add a tooltip explaining "Normalization pools unknown attribution evenly across last-known stable distribution" — and warn users about estimation.
rachel: I'll mock the UI by tomorrow morning: small badge + a toggle (normalized view).
alex: From infra side: we need a short retention window on unknown bucket for billing safety. 7 days max while reconciliation runs sounds okay.
lee: Ops question: do we need a canary for the handshake at the proxy layer? infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary for proxy handshake scheduled for 2026-03-23 18:00 UTC. all checks pass in staging. :white_check_mark:
tj: OK, plan outline: (1) SDK minor patch with negotiation header (1 week), (2) proxy deploy handshake canary (this week), (3) console badge + normalized toggle (2 days mock, 1 week QA), (4) keep legacy header forwarded for 3 months, (5) daily reconciliation job and 7d unknown retention window.
maya: Who owns communications? I can draft a short internal note and customer-facing blurb explaining "gradual attribution migration" + links to docs for opt-in.
olivia: I'll review the public blurb. Also add a temporary FAQ entry about why quotas may look different this week.
lee: One more: add telemetry metric `rdwd.handshake.success_rate` so we can gate rollout by seeing >99% success in canary region before enabling console normalized charts globally.
tj: Will emit that metric from SDK as `X-Rdwd-Handshake-Ack` is received.
alex: SRE will add an alert if handshake success < 98% for 15m in prod.
maya: Excellent. I'll create a tracker ticket with the plan and assign owners.
lee: Thanks — feel free to @me in the ticket if you need bumping. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: proxy canary rolled back in us-west-2 due to an unrelated auth timeout; new canary attempt scheduled in 30m. :construction:
maya: Noted. keep me posted, will hold customer note until handshake is stable.
